bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' and 'capital efficiency'; Celebratory of hitting FCF positive early; Pragmatic on competition (dismisses Amazon 3PL threat as 'old news'); Forward-looking on automation to counter labor tightness.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly states that 1P logistics is structurally more expensive than 3P even after margins, suggesting a long-term structural shift of volume back to 3P as marketplaces face regulatory/labor cost pressures; The 'Delhivery Direct' app is quietly capturing significant SME/D2C share outside of aggregator channels; FCF positivity achieved despite full-year Ecom Express integration costs.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Employee stock options are a stated part of the compensation structure: as of Jun 30, 2026, ESOPs granted comprise 61,07,155 vested (unexercised) shares (0.8% of shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis) and 1,58,33,027 unvested (2.0%).
- An additional ungranted pool is disclosed — time-based ESOPs of 1,71,67,822 shares (2.1% fully diluted) and performance-based ESOPs of 1,59,00,000 shares (2.0% fully diluted).
- Performance-based ESOPs are tied to share-price milestones: to be unlocked in three equal tranches upon achieving share prices of ₹800, ₹1,000 and ₹1,200, and vest equally over 2 years thereafter; time-based ESOP vesting typically ranges from 3 to 4 years from the date of grant.
- The estimated non-cash P&L charge for ESOPs already granted is given as ₹139 Cr in FY27, ₹94 Cr in FY28, ₹42 Cr in FY29 and ₹7 Cr in FY30, with a deck-stated total of ₹283 Cr (reversible in the event of forfeiture upon resignation/termination prior to completion of vesting).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated single network: Express Parcel and Part Truckload run on the same gateways, line-haul and sortation infrastructure, letting capacity be shared across business lines and giving PTL shippers e-commerce-like turnaround times on several lanes
- Proprietary in-house logistics operating system with over 80 applications, plus configurable APIs and libraries that internal and external developers build on
- Data intelligence and machine learning across geo-location, network design, route optimisation, load aggregation, ETA prediction, product identification and fraud detection, drawing on fifteen years of proprietary shipment and telemetry data
- Automation scale: 47 fully and semi-automated sortation centres, 129 gateways and 10.4 million shipments/day rated automated sort capacity, with machine-vision guided truck loading and system-directed floor operations
- Network reach and density: services in 18,830 PIN codes covering approximately 97% of India's deliverable addresses, 71,362 partner agents and 52K+ active customers
- Asset-light model with no real-estate ownership and only part of the deployed fleet owned, using managed marketplaces to match partner capacity to demand — lower fixed cost and flexibility to seasonal swings
- Scale leadership: largest third-party Express Parcel network by volume and second-largest player in Express PTL, reinforced by the Ecom Express integration which added density, route viability and lower marginal cost per incremental parcel
- Experienced entrepreneurial team drawn from engineering, technology, operations, R&D and design across industries
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Fuel price volatility with imperfect pass-through — Fuel is a major portion of transportation cost and diesel prices track imported crude. Management notes pass-through is handled through contractual fuel price adjustment mechanisms that may operate with a time lag, may have defined thresholds or caps, and may not fully offset sudden or sustained volatility.
- Geopolitical shocks to crude oil supply — Conflicts in the Middle East and disruption around transit routes such as the Strait of Hormuz have sharpened oil-price uncertainty; after the U.S.-Iran conflict broke out in February 2026 Brent rose over 60% from about US$72/bbl to a peak near US$118/bbl in March 2026 before moderating to about US$93/bbl by August 2026, feeding into Indian diesel and petrol prices in May 2026. Management also flags that FY27 has started with significant geopolitical risk.
- Seasonal blue-collar workforce migration — Migration during harvesting and election periods creates delivery delays and higher dwell time at hubs, forcing idle-capacity overheads and premium costs for emergency temporary staff; reliance on a transient workforce is described as a structural risk to service-level agreements and long-term supply-chain stability.
- Truck driver shortage — Drivers find the profession unattractive because of weak security and safety, harsh conditions, irregular hours and long time away from families, constraining line-haul capacity even as road infrastructure and ADAS-type technology improve conditions.
- Reverse logistics and return cost in e-commerce — Customer returns create complexity around pick-up timing, communication with pick-up personnel and packaging, adding cost for sellers and weighing on the growth economics of e-commerce logistics.
- Last-mile connectivity constraints — Manpower availability, inadequate road infrastructure, traffic congestion, poor address mapping and weather disruptions cause delays, higher cost and lower customer satisfaction in the last mile, which matters most for e-commerce and FMCG shippers.
- Highly fragmented Indian logistics industry — Numerous small players operating independently across supply-chain segments cause suboptimal resource utilisation, lack of standardisation and coordination difficulties — a structurally competitive, low-standardisation market that organised players must consolidate through technology platforms, logistics parks and hubs.
- Regulatory and labour-cost change — The Unified Labour Code implementation of November 2025 consolidates 29 labour laws into four codes, universalises minimum wages and extends social security to gig and platform workers; together with the September 2025 GST 'Next-Gen' two-slab reform and April 2026 CBIC courier-export reforms, the compliance and cost base of a large contractual and partner-agent workforce is exposed to statutory change.

business.body:
- [Ecom Express] The deck repeatedly carves out integration costs of the acquired Ecom Express business, quantified as ₹90 Cr for Q2FY26, ₹35 Cr for Q3FY26, ₹22 Cr for Q4FY26, ₹17 Cr for Q1FY27 and ₹148 Cr for FY26, described as net temporary costs pertaining to infrastructure, people, overheads, and business to be discontinued.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Delhivery runs a pan-India integrated logistics network spanning Express Parcel, Part Truckload, Supply Chain Services, Full Truckload, International and Local services, offering door-to-door parcel delivery, B2B freight, warehousing and fulfilment, cross-border shipping, intracity delivery and supply-chain software. Its customers are e-commerce marketplaces, direct-to-consumer brands, SMEs, consumer-to-consumer senders and enterprise shippers across FMCG, consumer durables, consumer electronics, lifestyle, retail, automotive and manufacturing, with value-added services such as forward and reverse logistics, cash-on-delivery management, payment collection and fraud detection. The model is asset-light: Delhivery invests in critical service elements, automation and IP-sensitive parts of the network while delivering much of the physical capacity through network partners and last-mile partner agents, all orchestrated by a self-developed logistics operating system.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Express Parcel:** Door-to-door parcel delivery across India, Forward and reverse logistics, Cash-on-delivery management, Nationwide fulfillment
- **Part Truckload:** Express B2B part-truckload freight, Appointment-based deliveries, Freight on Delivery (FOD), Freight on Pickup (FOP), Electronic Proof of Delivery (e-POD)
- **Supply Chain Services:** Integrated warehousing (fulfilment) and transportation, Multi-tenant and dedicated Fulfilment Centres
- **Full Truckload:** Point-to-point and multi-point FTL services, Orion (asset-light freight exchange), Freight Index One (FTL pricing intelligence platform)
- **International:** International parcel shipping, Freight forwarding, Customs clearance and shipment visibility, Air-parcel service for SME and enterprise exports
- **Local:** Delhivery Local (on-demand intracity logistics), Delhivery Rapid (2-4 hour intra-city fulfilment)
- **Software:** Supply chain software / logistics software as a service

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Grow share in the core Express Parcel and Part Truckload businesses by adding network volume, since higher volumes make more routes viable for faster and cost-efficient delivery and deepen the operating leverage of the integrated model
- Use the completed Ecom Express integration to hold client volumes, densify coverage, improve route viability, speed up delivery and absorb additional volume at lower marginal cost
- Build out new service lines — Delhivery Local (on-demand intracity), Delhivery Rapid (2-4 hour intra-city fulfilment) and Delhivery International — and keep investing behind them
- Keep technology and engineering at the core: in-house logistics operating system, proprietary data intelligence, LLM and multimodal AI across voice, vision, location intelligence and real-time transaction processing, SOP2Code/Spec2Code pipelines and a purpose-built agentic harness, moving towards in-house AI maps and 'physical AI'
- Continue operationalising and upgrading automated infrastructure — extending the work at the three mega-gateways (Tauru, Lonad, Hoskote) and inducting newer material-handling systems, high-speed sorters, AGVs and ASRS — explicitly to raise throughput and reduce exposure to wage inflation and labour availability constraints
- Develop in-house software and integrated hardware for mobile robotics and truck loading/unloading automation through the R&D team set up in FY26, targeted at pallet movement and lower truck turnaround time
- Invest in homegrown talent: convert contractual workers into permanent roles, promote from within, and expand training through the Delhivery Academy and the Skill Development Programme
- Expand welfare and inclusion — the Abhayam benefits programme for the 1 lakh-plus frontline workforce, living wages, and more opportunities for women including all-women hubs
- Run an asset-light model that invests in critical service elements and IP-sensitive parts of the network while delivering physical capacity through a large partner network operated as a managed marketplace
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Delhivery's capital expenditure is directed at fit-out infrastructure, state-of-the-art automation and IT assets, and tractor-trailers; automation covers parcel sorter systems, bag sortation systems and conveyance systems plus future-ready technologies such as automatic guided vehicles, automatic storage and retrieval systems and unmanned aerial vehicles. The company owns no real estate and only a portion of the fleet deployed in its network, so spend is deliberately concentrated on critical service elements and IP-sensitive parts of the network while physical capacity is delivered through partners. During FY26 it capitalised Rs 4,933.26 million of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets (excluding additions through acquisition and disposals), carried Rs 9.67 million of capital work in progress at year end, and funded the programme entirely through internal accruals and available cash; capex intensity fell from 5.2% of revenue in FY25 to 4.7% in FY26. The named FY26 projects were the expansion of mid-mile facilities in Chandigarh, Gurgaon, Ludhiana, Patna, Jaipur, Ahmedabad, Guwahati, Pune, Cochin, Lucknow, Goa, Purnia and Rudrapur, and the deployment of 123 additional 46ft tractors to raise the share of tractor-trailer capacity in the linehaul network. Automated material handling systems run at the Bhiwandi (Maharashtra), Tauru (Haryana) and Bengaluru (Karnataka) gateways, leaving 47 fully and semi-automated sortation centres, 129 gateways, 158 processing centres, 99 fulfilment centres (7.5 Mn sq ft of warehousing under management) and 4,848 last-mile distribution centres at 31 March 2026. On the inorganic side, Delhivery acquired 100.0% of Ecom Express, the #3 independent express player in India, for a consideration of about Rs 1,371 crore, aimed at cementing its position as the No. 1 independent express parcel player; one-time integration costs covered shutdown of redundant facilities, dismantling and transfer of automation equipment, exit from contracts and employee exits. Fleet and energy investment continued: 123 tractors added taking the tractor fleet to 624, 30 more LNG tractors taking that fleet to 50, over 3,000 contracted CNG- or electricity-powered vehicles in first-mile, carting and last-mile operations, and installed solar capacity of 5 MW at the end of FY26 which the company aims to augment during FY27. Liquidity to fund further organic and inorganic growth stood at Rs 45,553.32 million of cash and treasury investments against outstanding borrowings of Rs 25.35 million, with capital commitments (net of advances) of Rs 1,373.86 million contracted at 31 March 2026.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Formalisation of India's logistics market: customers are consolidating supply-chain spend with integrated 3PLs that offer reliability, visibility and nationwide reach, which management says drove share gains across all service lines in FY26
- Operating leverage compounding at scale — rising volumes plus a steadily improving cost structure from years of automation and network engineering investment, and added volume density post the Ecom Express integration; EBITDA margin moved from 1.6% in FY24 to 4.2% in FY25 to 6.1% in FY26
- India macro: IMF puts India as the fastest-growing large economy with growth around 6.5% in 2025 and 2026, nominal GDP of Rs 351 trillion (US$4.1 trillion) in FY2026, inflation around 4.7% in 2026, and consumption-led growth with PFCE rising as a share of GDP
- Market size and mix: total India logistics market of US$247-270 billion in FY25, with road transportation holding around 66% of cargo movement by tonnage; global logistics market growing at a 10.7% CAGR to US$18.23 trillion by 2030
- Rising consumer incomes — GNI per capita compounding ~9.3% between FY2020-2025, high- and middle-income households up from ~174 million in FY2020 to ~218 million in FY2025 with ~55 Mn more projected by FY2030
- Digital adoption: online shoppers projected to grow 8-10% CAGR from FY2025 to 365-430 million by FY2030, aided by cheap smartphones and among the lowest data costs globally
- New B2C commerce models — social commerce, omnichannel, quick commerce and D2C — plus category expansion into consumer durables, home and furniture, increasing demand for reliable organised logistics
- Evolving B2B models (direct-to-retail, direct-to-consumer) and government programmes like Make in India and PLI, driving demand for speed, precision and visibility in B2B supply chains
- Post-GST demand for integrated warehousing, transportation and technology from a single provider rather than mono-line players, plus growth of Tier 2 and beyond favouring players with deep national capabilities
- Technology-led transformation of the industry — automated sortation, AMRs, ASRS, wider WMS penetration, connected logistics/IoT and 5G, and AI in supply chain operations for large nationwide networks
- Headwind acknowledged by management: a challenging macro backdrop at the end of FY26 from geopolitical tensions affecting crude oil prices, with FY27 starting with significant geopolitical risk

deepdive.thesis: Delhivery delivered a bellwether FY26 with >1B parcels shipped and a decisive pivot to free cash flow positivity (Rs 89 Cr) one year ahead of schedule, driven by record volumes in Express/PTL and a margin turnaround in Supply Chain. The core thesis shifts from growth-at-all-costs to capital-efficient scaling, with ROIC expanding to 16% and net working capital compressing to 11 days, validating the operating leverage of the integrated network.

open.item: Shift intra-city fleet from spot to long-term fixed contracts to lock in rates for next year and avoid peak-season cost spikes.
Rs. 7 crore additional oxygen-concentrator recovery expected over the next four to six quarters (Rs. 21 cr of Rs. 28 cr already recovered/reversed).
~Rs.3 diesel/pump price increase to be passed through via diesel-price-hike clauses (already showing in air-shipping Rs.1-2 increases); some near-term consumption headwind possible.
Merging the rapid and non-rapid (express) networks to improve rapid-commerce profitability, expected to start playing out by Q1 of next FY.
AGV pilots in mega gateways (Bombay) to scale up / expand to other mega gateways within this year, driven by tightening labor; not material to capex trajectory.
New-initiative (Delhivery Direct, Rapid, cross-border, financial services) investment guided at ~Rs. 130-160 crore over the next year.
New mid-size facilities in Chennai, Hyderabad (Medchal) and Noida built with a 3-4 year horizon, expected to last until fiscal 2027.
Overall adjusted EBITDA (6.3% transport in FY26) has potential to reach at least ~10%-11% of revenue (Express+PTL ~18%, corporate overheads to ~7%).
Corporate overheads expected to decline to ~7% of revenue (from ~9%) as part of the adjusted-EBITDA improvement path.
No single-customer concentration concern until a customer crosses ~35% of revenue (largest was 16% last year, now higher but well below 35%).
E-commerce industry expected to grow 15%-20% into the medium term (Delhivery a downstream beneficiary).
Capex intensity (4.7% in FY26, down from 7.8% FY23) expected to reach the ~4% target; AI and robotics investments will not materially alter the trajectory.
SCS pipeline (breakeven achieved, service EBITDA 4x to Rs.79 cr) to remain margin-accretive with every new client meeting an internal hurdle rate.
Transport ROIC (16% in FY26) targeted to reach 25%+ in steady state, driven by margin expansion and ~2-3 pts capital-intensity improvement.
PTL service EBITDA margin expected to keep expanding toward ~18% (a key driver of ROIC improvement).
Building utilization-indexed / dynamic (route-, time-, weight-, client-based) pricing to give lane discounts while improving profitability; expected to be solved over the next couple of quarters.
Delhivery will not unbundle/disintermediate its integrated network to participate in third-party platforms (e.g. Valmo).

verdicts.note: Vivek cites corporate overheads going down to '7% of revenue' in the ROIC bridge - on the glide path but target now framed nearer 7% (still above 6%).

verdicts.item: PTL service EBITDA margin (3.8% in Q3, highest in 11 quarters) expected to keep improving, at a faster pace than Express.
verdicts.note: 'PTL margins expanded again successively'; gross margins 14% to 28% - continued improvement toward Express-level.

verdicts.item: PTL service EBITDA margins expected to rise from +3% to the +15%/+16% range as volumes grow, mirroring Express; yield improvements would be additive.
verdicts.note: PTL margins 'expanded again successively'; Vivek 'PTL getting closer to 18%'; gross margin 28% - progressing toward/through 15-16% with yield additive, not explicitly at target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Internal ambition to grow the PTL business ~25%-30% in FY26, well above the flattish/low-single-digit industry.
verdicts.note: FY26 PTL revenue +~19% / volume +~18%; Q4 +20% - strong but below the 25-30% internal ambition (in line with the revised ~20% guidance). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Express Parcel steady-state service EBITDA margins expected to remain in the 17%-20% range (18%-20% reiterated), potentially higher if price discounts no longer needed.
verdicts.note: Express 'firmly at the upper end' of the 16-18% range (~18%), within the 17-20% steady-state expectation.

wtt.summary: 51% guidance hit (34 chains); 1/2 projects on-time; 6 expired; 15% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Very confident; management touted beating the FCF plan by a year and reiterated long-term margin/ROIC targets, with no misses acknowledged.
